ImageDescription.value:
A very lucky shot, as it would have been impossible a few seconds either way! It's also a very rare vehicle - the Celica Camry was JDM only, and was basically a Carina with the Celica engine and front end. It's also the car that gave birth to the legendary and long-running Camry nameplate.

This one was piloted by a smartly dressed older chap, who I suspect has been the only NZ owner since the car was imported from Japan in 1988.

identity_evidence.source_market: Japan domestic only vehicle imported into New Zealand, explicitly stated by original photographer; not a claim of Russian original delivery
identity_evidence.body_generation: 1982 Toyota Celica Camry TA46 XT Super Edition four-door sedan; Japanese A40/A50 family, not later FWD Camry V10
identity_evidence.front_config: Drom Japanese A40/A50 RA55/TA46 group and source both show separate rectangular headlamp assemblies, black T-divider grille, front wing mirrors, thin pillars and four-door sedan body. Selected XT source differs in trim/badging from catalog GT photograph, retained as XT representative; no conversion to GT.
identity_evidence.visual_observation: 实际1920派生原图完整显示1982 Celica Camry TA46 XT Super Edition四门三厢、窄黑T字分格格栅及矩形复合灯/橙角灯、翼子板双镜、车身细条、圆形银轮罩和全部可见轮胎。前方半透视，前脸占比偏高但两扇侧门和纵向完整车身清楚，非后方/纯侧面。动态拍摄但车体和轮罩结构可辨；保持实际前轮轻微转向，不宣称静态OEM认证。
identity_evidence.market_applicability: Exact JDM-only A40/A50 Celica Camry exterior represented by Japanese original imported to NZ, corroborated by photographer and Drom Japan-only catalog. Frozen task Celica Camry contains no Russia-only trim restriction; no statement that picture was taken in Russia.
